questions.question: Which description fits the **EventDefinition** resource?
options: This resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur.
A structured set of questions intended to guide the collection of answers from end-users.
A kind of specimen with associated set of requirements.
This resource allows for the definition of some activity to be performed, independent of a particular patient, practitioner, or other performance context.
questions.explanation: **EventDefinition**: The EventDefinition resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur. The other descriptions belong to **Questionnaire**, **SpecimenDefinition**, **ActivityDefinition**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “This resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur.”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **EventDefinition** (Specialized › Definitional Artifacts).

questions.question: Where does **EventDefinition** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **EventDefinition** is in **Specialized › Definitional Artifacts**: Reusable templates that define things before they happen: protocols and order sets (PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition), forms (Questionnaire), and definitions of observations, specimens, devices and events.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **EventDefinition** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of EventDefinition are `status` (1..1), `trigger` (1..*). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **EventDefinition** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of EventDefinition: `status`. `status`: draft | active | retired | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
